subject: Renewal + capacity uplift — request for timebound price hold
messages:
From: Samir Khan <samir@thriveai.co>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal conversation + procurement window

Hi Priya,

Quick note as we start budgeting for H2 — our renewal for Redwood is up at the end of June. Procurement has asked us to lock pricing for 60 days while they finish Q3 approvals. Given our anticipated usage (we're planning to increase inference capacity ~50% for the recommendation pipeline), I wanted to check whether you can offer a short-term price hold and an uplift discount if we commit to an increased baseline.

Things that matter to us:
- A 60-day price hold while procurement completes approvals (no rate increases during that window)
- Discounted overage or a committed uplift to cover the 50% growth (ideally a blended discount)
- A simple amendment/PO we can route through legal and procurement quickly

Procurement timeline: PO and legal sign-off target by 2027-06-07.

Can we discuss options tomorrow? I can loop in our procurement and legal contacts if that helps.

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Khan
CTO, ThriveAI
samir@thriveai.co
+1 415-555-0198
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir@thriveai.co>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation + procurement window

Samir — thanks for the heads up and the clear timeline. I pulled some initial options together for a quick path to PO. High level proposal below; attaching a draft amendment for procurement to start reviewing. (See: ThriveAI_Renewal_Draft_Amendment_v1.pdf)

Option A — Rapid (preferred for procurement)
- 60-day guaranteed price hold on current list rates
- 12-month term extension from renewal date
- 25% committed uplift (covers ~50% of peak growth while keeping buffer)
- 10% discount on incremental committed units (applies to uplift portion)
- Overage rate tier with a 7% cap for first 90 days after uplift activates

Option B — Stronger concession (requires leadership approval)
- 60-day price hold + 6-month fixed pricing after PO
- 18-month term + 50% committed uplift
- 15% discount on uplifted portion

Next steps I recommend:
1) Procurement reviews the attached amendment and confirms any mandatory clauses (PO template, invoicing cadence).
2) If Option A looks acceptable, I can get Ben to finalize commercial terms and route to legal for a fast-signature addendum.
3) If they prefer Option B we escalate to Leadership — Ben, could you weigh in on margin / approval runway?

Attaching draft amendment for review. Happy to jump on a 20-min call tomorrow morning.

— Priya
Priya Natarajan
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
priya_natarajan@redwood.com
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Samir Khan <samir@thriveai.co>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation + procurement window

Priya / Samir — looping in Vivek for the capacity / dedicated ask. Quick commercial read from my side: we can comfortably support Option A without escalation. Option B (15% + 50% uplift + 6-month fixed) is possible but needs a quick sign-off from Sales Leadership due to margin impact.

My recommended practical counter (to speed procurement):
- Accept Option A structure with altered numbers: 30% committed uplift (to better cover their projected growth)
- Offer 12% discount on the uplift (midpoint between A and B)
- Provide a 90-day overage cap at 5% above agreed uplift before tier kicks in

I've attached a simple pricing model showing blended unit economics for both options (pricing-model.xlsx). If Samir can confirm the target uplift number (exact units / seat / inference-hours) we'll plug it in and I can produce a final amendment for signature.

Ben Carter
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Khan <samir@thriveai.co>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation + procurement window

Thanks for the context. Two operational constraints to flag so procurement/legal know what to expect:

1) Dedicated capacity / reserved GPU pools: if ThriveAI wants the uplift to map to reserved capacity (recommended for latency predictability), we need a 60-day lead time to provision new capacity or reassign pool quotas. That means an uplift effective date potentially pushed out unless they accept burstable shared capacity in the interim.

2) Price holds: we can lock list pricing for 60 days, but deeper discounts tied to reserved capacity require a minimum committed spend profile (we can document a commitment schedule in the amendment). Also for a 6-month fixed pricing window (Option B) Finance needs a clear committed baseline and signed term extension before the fixed window starts.

If procurement needs samples of the capacity SLA/annex, I can drop a short operational addendum into the draft for legal. Priya — happy to sync for 15 minutes to confirm uplift units and provisioning timeline.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Product Ops, Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
From: Samir Khan <samir@thriveai.co>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@thriveai.co>, Legal - ThriveAI <legal@thriveai.co>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Jun 2027 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation + procurement window

Thanks everyone — this is helpful. Procurement reviewed Option A with Ben's tweak (30% uplift + 12% discount on uplift) and asked for the following to move quickly:

- A one-page amendment they can attach to the PO (we will route to legal).
- Confirmation that the 60-day price hold is in writing and that overage caps apply as outlined.
- A DocuSign-ready amendment and a sample PO template (so procurement can cross-check invoicing fields).

Ben/Priya — if you can send a DocuSign-ready PDF and I can get our legal team to review Monday morning, procurement is aiming to sign by 2027-06-07. I'm attaching our PO template for reference (PO_template.pdf).

If possible could Redwood confirm provisioning lead time for the uplift if we add reserved capacity? Vivek's note on 60-day lead time is understood; if we need to start with burstable capacity to avoid a gap, we can do that as an interim.

I'll expect the final amendment link and a HubSpot deal note so our procurement team can verify the commercial terms.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — looking forward to finalizing.

Best,
Samir
